text.p: New South Wales coal miner Centennial Coal Co Ltd said on Friday raw coal production in the December quarter rose to 372,000 tonnes and saleable output to 334,000 tonnes, up 14 percent and 5.0 percent over the comparable quarter last year, aided by productivity gains.
Centennial said sales from its own mines increased 27 percent to 405,000 tonnes with total group sales, including "traded" coal, of 413,000 tonnes.
The latest quarter's sales have been the strongest since August 1994, Centennial said.

"Such sales have, however, been attained in a difficult trading environment with both local and export prices under pressure and lower sales volumes to the building materials sector," the company said.
The recent settlement of export coking and semi-soft coal prices has not assisted the climate for the current steaming coal price negotiations with the Japanese power utilities, Centennial said.
"Unfortunately, it appears likely that export prices will be reduced from current levels for the coming Japanese fiscal year to 31 March 1998."
Australian steaming coal producers have settled with Japan for a price cut of US$2.60 to US$2.70 a tonne for exports in the 1997/98 fiscal year, senior coal industry sources told Reuters on Thursday.
